q: What do we know about ds-csb-oot-2025q1 in the churn-small-business project?
a: It is the SMB holdout: 8,914 accounts from the Jan to Mar 2025 snapshots with 90-day labels maturing by 2025-06-30 and 7.1% churn; the tree models are scored on its 7,930-account subset with 6 or more months of tenure.

q: What came of the unresolved-calls feature in the churn-small-business project (exp-205 and exp-207)?
a: exp-205 on the first calls build showed +0.012 AUC, but duplicate call_ids inflated it; after the dedupe in exp-207 the lift was +0.002 AUC, so the feature stayed in csb-xgb-v2 as a small signal (fnd-csb-calls-lift-v2).

q: What does csb-xgb-v2 in the churn-small-business project use as inputs?
a: Five features: feat-csb-spend-sa-v2, feat-csb-deposit-volatility, feat-csb-tenure-band, employee-card count and feat-csb-calls-unresolved, trained on accounts with 6 or more months of tenure with 90-day labels.

q: What is the current scoring model in the churn-small-business project?
a: csb-xgb-v2, shipped for the April 2026 cycle by dec-csb-ship-xgb-v2; it replaces csb-xgb-v1, the December 2025 pilot model.

q: What AUC does csb-xgb-v2 reach on the csb-oot-2025q1 holdout in the churn-small-business project?
a: 0.758 on the 7,930-account subset with 6 or more months of tenure (KS 0.40, recall@10% 0.31).

q: Why does the churn-small-business project use 90-day labels rather than 60-day labels?
a: SMB spend is seasonal, so 60-day windows label quiet months as churn; the 90-day window gave 0.684 AUC against 0.671 and a 7.1% base rate on the holdout (exp-201), recorded in dec-csb-90d-window.
